findings.subject: Area A South Transverse Chamber: deliberately placed large stones
findings.assertion: In the South Transverse Chamber, excavators reported several large, harder stones unlike the smaller rocks embedded in the surrounding matrix. Altschul and Drewitt excavated underneath to check whether the stones were bedrock or fill, finding the stones resting on soil rather than embedded. No equivalent deliberately placed stones were reported in the North pit. The suggestion that the chamber was additionally hollowed out to place them is an inference.
findings.geography: Area A South pit, cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.source_locator: Sload 2020 printed p.97, Figure 7.1 on printed p.99; quotes Altschul 1978a:45,50,52–53; PDF images inspected at zero-index 120 and 122
findings.evidence_type: published excavation discussion, field photograph and plan
findings.confidence: moderate for report of stratigraphic observation; low for inferred human purpose
findings.limitations: The underlying Altschul 1978 field notebook and stones not directly inspected; published 2020 account is not independent corroboration.

findings.subject: Area D entrance: stratigraphic relationship of Teotihuacan step, cave fill and later concrete floor
findings.assertion: At the western cave entrance, Area D excavations showed a concrete floor that reached just below and several centimeters above the base of an existing Teotihuacan step but did not extend beneath it. The underlying cascajo Layer 3 deposits became thinner near the step. Figure 7.4 distinguishes a modern packed dirt surface (Layer 1), a Teotihuacan concrete floor (Layer 2), underlying Layer 3 deposits including a fire pit, and a lower compacted earthen floor (field Layer 3c), above lower tepetate/cascajo fill. The relationship supports construction of concrete flooring relative to the step but does not establish an exact building date.
findings.period: Teotihuacan early centuries CE, dating uncertain; excavated 1978
findings.geography: Area D entrance step, Sun Pyramid cave, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.source_locator: Sload 2020 printed pp.100–103, Figures 7.3 and 7.4; PDF screenshots zero-index 123,124,126; Altschul 1978a:153–164 referenced but not directly reviewed
findings.evidence_type: photographic cave entrance survey and excavation stratigraphic section
findings.confidence: moderate for documented stratigraphy; timing and intention unresolved
findings.limitations: Sload's model reconciles some field layer numbers to new numbering; 1978 original sheets unavailable. Beta 220763/220764 sample assignments cannot alone date the stone step.

proposed_enrichments.assertion: Area A Beta 220745 was a charcoal band several cm beneath concrete, extending 17 cm into cascajo; no ash or soil discoloration reported; at least one piece of charcoal measured 5 cm across. Such a deposit is not automatically a preserved in-place hearth.
